author: TEDx Talks
description: What makes for an incredible sexual experience? Is it advanced technique or the ability to contort your body into a pretzel? Is it the rush of the honeymoon phase? No... and no. So what is it? One day, as a client described the kind of sex they longed for – sex that made the world around them disappear – I realized they were describing something familiar: a flow state. You know the feeling. A surfer who becomes one with the wave. A musician lost in the music. These are experiences that yield a sense of timelessness, total absorption, and merger. But no one was talking about this in the context of sex. So, being an evidence-based practitioner, I turned to the research and found… nothing. No studies. No theory. No guidebook. So, I conducted my own first-of-its-kind study exploring the link between flow and sexual satisfaction. What I found blew me away: couples who experienced flow reported deeper intimacy, higher desire, and more satisfying sex far beyond what those described in the ho
title: How to have sex that keeps getting better | Emily Jamea | TEDxThird Ward

author: TEDx Talks
description: In his talk, ByLwansta explores the importance of alternatives in shaping healthy societies. Drawing from his work as an artist, creative entrepreneur, and co-founder of Your Weekly Touch Up, he challenges dominant narratives by creating space for alternative ways of seeing, creating, and belonging. Situating himself within the crevices of what he describes as South Africa's "gradient society," he invites audiences to look more closely, listen more attentively, and embrace the richness that exists beyond the mainstream. In this context, he argues that alternatives are not simply another option, but an essential condition for cultural evolution and meaningful transformation. ByLwansta is a South African artist-entrepreneur and cultural producer. His work spans music, design, curation, and infrastructure building. He is driven by a simple philosophy: creating the things he wishes existed. His work prioritises storytelling, world-building, and long-term cultural infrastructure over monet
title: Why societies need alternatives to survive | By Lwansta | TEDxJohannesburg Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
There's a particular kind of harmony that only twins seem able to produce not just musically, but in the way they move and breathe together on stage. Diya and Jiya have that in spades. Their journey through Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Li'l Champs Season 9 introduced them to national audiences, but it's the years since that have shaped them into performers who know exactly what a room needs. They don't just sing together; they build something between them and the audience a blend of emotion, discipline, and energy that turns a performance into a shared moment rather than a spectacle. At TEDxNHCE, that's exactly what they brought: melodies that lingered long after the last note, and a reminder that music, at its best, is never really about performance it's about connection.
 Diya and Jiya are dynamic twin performers whose soulful vocals and engaging presence have won hearts across digital platforms and live stages. Recognized for their remarkable journey as contestants on Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Li’l Champs
title: Voices That Connect | Diya and Jiya | TEDxNHCE

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, speaker Rishab Thosani dives into the wonderful world of AI. Starting from the basic fundamentals to advanced future applications, Mr. Thosani explains why and how we are trending towards a future that is increasingly sycophantic.  Junior and Bellaire High School student Rishabh Thosani has a passion for machine learning and AI research, having built and trained neural networks from scratch using PyTorch. This summer, he will be joining UT Dallas's Multimodal Interactions Lab as a research intern, working on haptics, VR, and human-computer interaction. Alongside his academic pursuits, Rishabh is the founder of Lectere, a startup where he puts his passion for technology into practice. As Co-President of Career Club and Vice President of Bollywood Club, he keeps himself busy both on and off the stage. In his free time, Rishabh enjoys binging K-dramas and finding new Monster Energy cans to add to his collection. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference f
title: Sycophancy and Seduction: the flattering side of modern AI | Rishabh Thosani | TEDxBellaire HS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: The System That Silences Children looks at how the family court system can overlook children's voices, even when they have important insight into their own situations. Sadie explores how therapists, mediators, and evaluators sometimes fail to truly listen, and how that gap can carry serious consequences for children's wellbeing and safety. She points to models like Scotland's, where courts are required to document how a child's views were gathered and considered, as an example of a more inclusive approach. Through her talk, Sadie shares how she helped support legislation that strengthens children's voices, and encourages audiences to see listening to children as both compassionate and necessary. Sadie Cohen is a senior at SRDS and is excited to give her first-ever TED Talk. She is deeply involved in child advocacy and is passionate about ensuring kids have a voice. Sadie recently testified on a bill to support children in the family court system, demonstrating her commitment to creati
title: The System that Silences Children | Sadie Cohen | TEDxSRDS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Sometimes music reaches places that words cannot. In this TEDx performance from Lagos, Algarve, Portugal, Sarah Donkor shares how music and movement can help us process emotion, reconnect with the body and come back to ourselves.

Joined on stage by students from her studio, Urban Dance Studio Lagos, Sarah brings this idea to life through rhythm, movement and shared energy. As she reminds us, music may not solve our problems, but it can bring us to a state where the mind is clearer, the body is calmer and the heart is more open to what is true. Dancer, Teacher, and Creative Entrepreneur

Sarah Donkor is a dancer, teacher, and creative entrepreneur whose work focuses on confidence, movement, and self-expression. Born in Belgium with Ghanaian and Algerian roots, and based in Portugal for the past ten years, she brings a multicultural perspective to everything she creates. She is also a mother of two, a role that deeply shapes her sense of purpose and resilience.

With years of experienc
title: Music as My Compass: Dance Performance | Sarah Donkor | TEDxPraça Gil Eanes

author: TEDx Talks
description:
As students move through the education system, learning often narrows just as their cognitive capacity expands. Success becomes about getting the right answer in the right way, in a predictable, controlled environment — while the world beyond school demands adaptability, persistence, and comfort with uncertainty.

Drawing on two decades as an educator, Nicole Dyson challenges the idea that young people are prepared for the future simply by mastering content or learning about resilience. As the founder of Future Anything, she designs learning experiences that deliberately place students inside moments of stretch, uncertainty and productive friction, helping tens of thousands of young people build the additional capability they need: agility.

Nicole reveals why the safest place for students to struggle might be the classroom — and why learning to navigate uncertainty is one of the most important skills we can teach. Nicole Dyson is a multi-award-winning educator and entrepreneur, worki
title: The power of productive friction | Nicole Dyson | TEDxBrisbane

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Maame's talk explores how adversity, pain, and unexpected life seasons are not interruptions — but invitations to transformation. Drawing from personal experiences and broader societal patterns, she challenges the idea that struggle is something to escape, and instead position it as a catalyst for purpose, leadership, and impact. She shares how reframing hardship can unlock gratitude, clarity, and direction. 

This talk invites individuals to rethink how they interpret their lowest moments. The core idea: what feels like breakdown may actually be divine or purposeful redirection. Maame De-Heer is a Lecturer, Research Lab Manager, Doctor of Public Health candidate and an Executive Director of Power of Love Foundation Canada. She is passionate about public health, equity, and youth empowerment, with a strong track record of global leadership, impactful research, and advocacy for mental health, Black health, and inclusive communities. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED con
title: The Ripple Effect of Academic Failure and Unshakeable Purpose. | Maame De-Heer | TEDxMississauga

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Have you ever reacted in a way that surprised you?

A small comment. A certain tone. A delayed reply. Suddenly, the moment feels bigger than it should. You get defensive. You shut down. You say something you wish you could take back. Later, you wonder, "Where did that come from?"

In this TEDx talk, neuroscientist Dr. Khai Win invites us to think again about our most automatic reactions. What if that moment you wish you could take back does not mean you are too emotional, too sensitive, or out of control? What if your brain was running an old pattern it learned from past experience?

Blending personal story with accessible neuroscience, Dr. Khai explores why some conversations feel personal before we even know why, moving us from self-blame to curiosity, and from old patterns to conscious choice.
This talk is for anyone ready to understand themselves differently. The Most Dangerous Software today Isn't AI.

References:
- Méndez-Bértolo et al. (2016). Nature Neuroscience.
https://pubme
title: What shapes our everyday decisions? | Dr. Khai Win | TEDxKew

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Lauren Pires was born with Central Core Disease, a rare neuromuscular disorder giving her 33% of the average person's physical strength - and hid her disability as much as she could for over 30 years. Convinced that resilience meant pushing through difficulties and pretending she was "normal," she avoided anything that might expose her limits - until she was forced to confront what hiding was actually costing her.

For over a decade, Lauren has lived by a simple but transformative practice she calls the Daily Yay: the intentional act of noticing and appreciating small moments of joy, not despite difficulties, but through them. Her idea worth spreading is that we don't build resilience by overcoming who we are, our difficult situations or things we can't change - we build it by working with what we have, and finding something to celebrate right where we are. 

Lauren's talk challenges the "triumph over adversity" narrative, invites audiences to stop waiting for things to be easier in o
title: How can we fit in without losing who we are? | Lauren Pires | TEDxMississauga

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Vaibhav's entire philosophy can be summed up in one sentence: fitness shouldn't be complicated, it should be sustainable. As the founder of AVG Runclub in Bengaluru, he's built something that looks like a running group on the surface but functions like a community a space where consistency matters more than intensity, and showing up matters more than perfection. His TEDxNHCE talk moved past workouts entirely, focusing on the mindset shift that turns fitness from a phase into a lifestyle. One run at a time, one habit at a time that's the whole idea, and it's worked for a lot of people who never thought of themselves as "runners."
 Vaibhav is the founder of Avg Run Club, a growing community focused on making running accessible, consistent, and engaging. With a shared vision of building more than just a fitness group, they have created a space where individuals come together to push limits, stay accountable, and support one another. Their approach emphasizes discipline, inclusivity, and
title: One Run at a Time | Vaibhav Kothari | TEDxNHCE

description:
Meera has spent over 25 years doing something most people underestimate until they need it desperately: teaching people how to speak so they're actually heard. As Founder & CEO of AASHA Infinite Foundation & FRH, she's trained more than 11,000 learners — a number that stops being abstract when you consider each one represents someone who walked in afraid to speak and walked out able to lead a room. Her TEDxNHCE talk was about exactly that transformation: how clarity, courage, and communication aren't soft skills, they're the difference between having an idea and having an impact.
 C V Meera Raman is a dynamic Communication Success Coach, Founder & CEO of AASHA Infinite Foundation & FRH, with 25+ years of experience empowering individuals to communicate with confidence and purpose. Having trained 11,000+ learners, she helps people overcome fear, build fluency, and unlock career success. Her mission is to create confident communicators who lead with clarity, courage, and impact. She tra
title: Turning Voices Into Opportunities | C V Meera Raman | TEDxNHCE

author: TEDx Talks
description:
My talk focuses on the tendency of minorities to hide who they really are in order to be accepted by society. In identity politics, who we are is ultimately the most important thing. By hiding certain aspects, changing who we are, lying to ourselves and the world. I want to drive the point of “be yourself” home, but back it up by actual evidence. "I'm not like them, I'm just like you"

Hi, I'm Alan, and I'm a second year student of the 2nd Highschool in Szczecin! I have already been a tedx speaker once, and found it to be one of the coolest things ever, which is why I'm doing it again this year. Outside of tedx events, I devote almost all of my time to MUNs - both delegating and chairing :). Additionally I love doing sports, drinking dubious amounts of coffee and doing the IB (rip). Hope to see you all at tedx! This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: "I'm not like them, I'm just like you" | Alan Tadeusz Olech | TEDxSecond HS Szczecin Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Occupational identity investigates how different roles one might have (like employee, manager etc.) interact in situations in the workplace and outside of it. It also examines the social rules that are forced on people as an result of these roles. For example let’s take a manager at a corporate chain, while working they might be angry towards their subordinates, they might come off as not respecting them. In fact it might be the contrary, outside of work they are friendly and pleasant to be around. The relationships that for because of this difference and how one might work to avoid or fall into these social constructs are what I’ll be talking about in my speech! ''How occupational identity shapes who we are and chose to become.''

Hey! I'm Tomek! For some time now I had been researching occupational identity, which is the study of how a person's job or what they do all day shape them. I can't wait to share what I learned with you and do that, while hopefully helping you better yourse
title: How occupational identity shapes who we are | Tomasz Jan Piątkowski | TEDxSecond HS Szczecin Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
- Being a third culture kid teaches you to adapt readily into many different and even new environments and yet, never be fully at home in any of them. This talk explores the advantages and disadvantages of growing up with multiple cultures and languages, and shows how one can make the best of it. It also reveals that actually everyone can feel this at times, even when they only come from one culture. "Home Is Everywhere — and Nowhere"

Hi, I’m Nathaniel! Truthfully doing a ted talk is a bit out of my comfort zone but I've never been one to shy away from a challenge. Being a third culture kid I sometimes find myself in unfamiliar situations and I hope to share some of what this feels like in my talk. In my free time I like sports, strength building, catching up with friends and eating ice cream, which I'm doing right now!!! This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: ''Home Is Everywhere — and Nowhere” | Nathaniel Gray | TEDxSecond HS Szczecin Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Careers today aren’t built in straight lines — they’re shaped by movement, change, and the ripple effects of our actions. 

In this talk, Jessica Tudos introduces the Cartwheel Career™ framework, a new way to design work and life through adaptability, momentum, and continuous reinvention. Drawing from her journey as an Olympian and life design strategist, she shows how embracing uncertainty and taking action can open unexpected opportunities. 

Her idea worth sharing: success is no longer about following a fixed path, but about building the capacity to keep moving and evolving. When we learn to “cartwheel” through our careers, we don’t just keep up with change—we create what comes next. Jessica Tudos, Olympian turned edupreneur, life design strategist, and speaker, champions the “portfolio mindset”—a future-proof approach to thriving with multiple passions. With 65+ jobs across 40+ countries, she inspires audiences to embrace curiosity, adaptability, and reinvention, empowering them t
title: Upside-down on Purpose: Why Movement is the New Stability | Jessica Tudos | TEDxMississauga

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Simone Arcagni propone un viaggio tra storia, cultura e immaginario, dimostrando come l'AI sia il risultato di idee, racconti e invenzioni che attraversano i secoli. Un nuovo punto di vista per leggere una delle tecnologie più trasformative del nostro tempo. Esperto di new media, intelligenza artificiale, cultura e arte digitale, attualmente, è docente presso l'Università IULM di Milano nel Dipartimento di Comunicazione, Arti e Media. I suoi studi si concentrano su nuovi media, intelligenza artificiale e tecnologie immersive, con particolare attenzione all'analisi culturale delle tecnologie digitali.

"Fresco" curatore della Biennale di Tecnologia del Politecnico di Torino, è stato docente all'Università di Palermo e, da giornalista, firma articoli per testate nazionali e internazionali.
Autore di articoli, saggi, monografie, alla produzione scientifica e accademica affianca un’ampia attività di consulente, curatore e divulgatore. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conf

description:
Confidence. Expression. Freedom. In this high-energy voguing performance, LeosDances and Horseontherunway celebrate individuality, challenge gender stereotypes, and bring the empowering spirit of ballroom culture to the TEDx stage with "Slay Your Life!" by RAGE! LeosDances is a viennese dancer and choreographer mainly in the styles such as Commercial, Voguing, Waacking and Heels but who always seeks to try new styles. Leo loves to tell stories and create memorable moments with the art of movement! His creative visions combine confident power with elegant sensuality, breaking gender stereotypes and inspiring others to be truly themselves!

Horseontherunway is a dancer who enjoys all things Vogue and kpop. In their personal time they like to enjoy a variety of video games and dvelve into fantasy worlds. author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the biggest barriers to your success were not visible? Not laws. Not circumstances. Not a lack of opportunity. But the invisible rules you've accepted without ever questioning them.

In "Living Beyond Invisible Rules," this thought-provoking TED Talk explores the hidden beliefs, cultural expectations, self-imposed limitations, and unspoken norms that quietly shape the decisions we make, the dreams we abandon, and the lives we settle for. Chloe Okulaja, Oluwatimisimi Afun, and Zarah Ibrahim form a dynamic trio united by curiosity, creativity, and ambition. Chloe is passionate about understanding human behaviour and challenging invisible social boundaries, while Timisimi brings creativity, leadership, and a strong sense of justice through her interests in art, music, business, and helping others. Zarah complements the group with her academic discipline, analytical thinking, and love for history and literature. Together, they combine intellect, creativity, and leadership to creat
title: Beyond Rules | Chloe Okulaja, Oluwatimisimi Afun, and Zarah Ibrahim (Trio) | TEDxGrange School Lagos

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We don't browse the internet — we are browsed by it. Increasingly, algorithms decide the next thing we'll do, and services eliminate all the friction between wanting and getting. But if everything slides toward us and we no longer have to move, is it still possible to feel enthusiasm for things?

If our cognition has gone sedentary, how do we get it moving again? And what does that have to do with reconnecting, building communities, and starting to imagine different futures? Born and raised on the internet, Matheus Sodré is a communicator, researcher, host, and screenwriter. Across short-form videos, long-form essays, his podcast (the "lan house," analog conversations about the digital world), and written pieces, he discusses culture, film, fashion, behavior, technology, and the future of things. He holds a degree in Social Communication from ESPM and is pursuing a master's in Creative Media at UFRJ's School of Communication. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conferenc
title: Imaginação Sedentária: Como Voltar a Sonhar | Matheus Sodré | TEDxBlumenau

author: TEDx Talks
description: In a world where everything competes for our attention, what can still bring us back to ourselves? In this talk, Taly Lima shares how she found in writing and slam poetry an exercise in presence. Taly Lima is a playwright, slammer, and arts educator. She investigates the spoken word as a tool for reclaiming the right to tell one's own stories. Between theater, slam poetry, and education, she creates spaces of listening where people can discover the power of their own voice. She is co-founder of Slam Descoloniza Blu and DENGO, initiatives that expand access to the word and to Black narratives. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description:
This talk challenges the culture of constant busyness in education, revealing how overloading ourselves leads to distraction and disconnection. It makes the case for doing less and slowing down in order to be fully present, showing how focus, connection, and meaningful learning grow when we give students our undivided attention. Vandy Moore has been teaching and learning alongside children for the
past 18 years. Throughout her career, Vandy has worked in every grade
level from Kindergarten through 6th grade, serving schools with a wide
range of demographics and needs.
Vandy is a graduate of Arkansas Tech University, where she earned both
her Bachelor’s Degree in Elementary Education and her Master’s Degree
in Special Education. She also holds an ESL endorsement.
In 2022 she was named the Russellville School District Teacher of the
Year.
Vandy is the founder and director of The School House, a microschool in
the Russellville area, where she currently teaches kindergarten.

title: Why slowing down is key to learning | Vandy Moore | TEDxCapitol View ED

description: In her TEDX Talk, "The Hidden Barriers in Women's Healthcare and Why Teenagers Are Stepping In," Priya sheds light on the systemic barriers women face in healthcare and explores why today's teenagers are breaking the stigma, advocating for change, and leading conversations that are shaping a more equitable future. Priya Senthilkumar is a 16-year-old incoming junior at McNeil High School and the founder of Herizon Health, a youth-led nonprofit focused on advancing women's healthcare education, advocacy, and community outreach. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Mari Moss explores how protecting people, culture, families, communities, and opportunity is the foundation of lasting prosperity. Drawing on her experience in economic development, public service, and her Lenape heritage, she demonstrates that the strongest economies are built by investing in human potential, preserving cultural legacy, expanding access to opportunity, and creating generational wealth.
 The Honorable Mari Moss, MPA is an economic developer, strategist, advocate, and community builder whose work advances equity, economic justice, and community preservation. A Lenape descendant with deep roots connected to Harlem, she brings a unique perspective on land, identity, and sustainable development.

As CEO of Midas Touch Consulting, Mari has supported more than $1 billion in development initiatives, helped create over 5,000 jobs, and advanced community-centered economic strategies, with nearly half of those opportunities benefiting Harlem. Her work focuses on expanding acces
title: The future is built by what we protect | Mari Moss | TEDxHarlem

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Even the most confident among us has moments when it feels like the balloon has deflated, when we think we can't do whatever is needed at the time. One day we believe we can conquer the world; the next day we feel alone and unsupported. What can we do to turn the energy around? How can we access our inner power and stand in our greatness? By remembering who we are, what makes us strong, what gives us value. By claiming our superpower. 
 Harriette Cole, founder of Harriette Cole Media, Inc., is a celebrated coach, bestselling author, storyteller, and media executive who has empowered entertainers, entrepreneurs, professionals, and students for more than 30 years. She is the author of seven books on personal growth and success and founded Dreamleapers to help people achieve their dreams. Cole hosts the radio show and podcast Dreamleapers with Harriette Cole and Dreamleapers Inspiration. She made history as the first female editor-in-chief of Ebony magazine and previously served as fashi
title: Confidence is Our Superpower | Harriette Cole | TEDxHarlem

description: Speaker Sebastian Camacho uses ancient philosophy to interpret, deconstruct, and address the stresses of modern day life, finding a unique angle in how to endure triggering moments in life.  Junior and Bellaire High school student-athlete Sebastian Camacho explores the integration of philosophy to everyday life, focusing on how mindset can affect the outcomes of stressful situations. Speaking from a stoic philosophical standpoint, Camacho is interested in applying ideas to daily modern challenges faced by the common student, particularly in high pressure environments. Camacho, in his free time, enjoys the outdoors, nature, and has a keen interest in wildlife. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description:
An analysis about the prevalence of wrongful conviction rates in Texas and the broader United States. Speaker Samantha Tran dives into some of the accessible ways to resolve the wrongful conviction crisis on a personal and national ways.  Senior and Bellaire High School student Samantha Tran is passionate about examining the complexities of the justice system while advocating for fairness, accountability, and reform. Through her TEDx talk on wrongful convictions in Texas, Tran sheds light on the systemic flaws, ranging from unreliable forensics to coercive plea bargains, that continue to impact lives and communities.

A dedicated debater and aspiring criminal lawyer since the third grade, Tran competes in Congressional Debate and aims to one day become the “Harvey Specter” of criminal law. As president of Student Council, she is committed to giving back to her community through leadership and service, while fostering civic engagement among her peers.
In her free time, Tran enjoys bing

description: A discussion about the implications of scientific skepticism in areas of public health, race relations, and media polarization. Speaker Ishani Kaushik weaves a personal account with a broader structural critique of modern polarity politics.  Junior and Bellaire High School student Ishani Kaushik aims to craft the intersection of neuroscience and immunology while advocating for healthcare justice and literacy for through the practice of journalism. Kaushik, a public speaking enthusiast, is an avid member of the Bellaire Speech and Debate team, where she competes in Informative Speaking. She also enjoys writing for her school’s newspaper, the Three Penny Press. In her free time, Kaushik loves making pasta, reading outdated Roman literature, or rewatching her favorite Bollywood movie. author: TEDx Talks
description: What does momentum look like when the world wasn't designed with you in mind? In this TEDx talk, Tanner Bergsma shares how his experiences with homelessness and autism shaped his understanding of resilience, challenging conventional ideas of success while exploring how more inclusive systems can help everyone move forward. Tanner Bergsma (they/them) is a Canadian autistic international bestselling author, TEDx speaker, and youth leader advancing mental health, inclusion, and systemic change on a global scale. With an academic background in psychology, Tanner combines lived experience, policy leadership, and frontline advocacy to drive meaningful, evidence-informed solutions. Tanner serves on multiple nonprofit and municipal boards, contributes to national initiatives, and represents Canadian and North American youth internationally. Tanner works with various Intergovernmental organizations to advance the Sustainable Development Goals and youth-driven policy, in order to strengthen com
title: The power of a 2:17 AM moment  | Tanner Bergsma | TEDxMcMasterU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the very thing you call strength is actually costing you everything?
For nearly two decades, Preetah Bolaky believed that handling everything alone, that is long nights, sheer willpower, never asking for help was what it meant to be strong. It got her from a bank clerk's desk to the boardroom as an Executive Director. But it also meant carrying every problem in silence, certain that asking for help was a sign of weakness.
Then she watched a senior leader with thirty years of experience do something she never expected: ask a junior colleague for their opinion. It made her question everything she believed about leadership and herself.
In this talk, Preetah shares the moment that changed how she sees strength, and why the people who rise the highest are rarely the ones who do it alone. Using the image of a fighter who never enters the ring without a corner, she makes the case that real strength isn't about having all the answers, it's about knowing you don't have to. Preetah Bola
title: The Leadership Habit That Earns More Respect, Not Less | Preetah Bolaky | TEDxKew
